title: One-Slip Mirror
statement: A sign maker wants every banner to read the same forwards and backwards, but allows fixing one slip: deleting at most one letter. Given text in lowercase letters, return true if it reads the same forwards and backwards after deleting at most one letter, and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: No single deletion makes a palindrome.

hints.content: Trying every single deletion and checking for a palindrome works but is quadratic.
Compare letters from both ends moving inward.
While the ends match, they can stay; the first mismatch is where the slip must be.
At the first mismatch, one of the two mismatched letters must be deleted.
Check whether the remaining middle is a palindrome after skipping the left letter, or after skipping the right letter. You only branch once.

testCases.explanation: No single deletion makes a palindrome.
One letter is already a palindrome.
Already a palindrome; no deletion needed.
Delete the last 'c'; skipping the wrong side first would fail.
After matching the outer letters, 'cd' needs one more deletion: delete c or d.
After matching a and b, the middle 'cxy' would need two deletions.

solutions.title: Try every deletion
solutions.intuition: Check the text itself and each version with one letter removed.
solutions.approach: Return true if text is a palindrome; otherwise test each one-letter deletion.
solutions.pseudocode: if pal(text): return true; for k: if pal(text without k): return true; return false
solutions.interviewExplanation: Trying each deletion is straightforward but builds and checks n strings of length n.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Deleting index 1 gives 'aca', which is a palindrome: return true.

solutions.title: Two pointers with one branch
solutions.intuition: Matching outer letters never need deleting, so the first mismatch decides which letter the slip could be.
solutions.approach: Move i and j inward while the letters match. On the first mismatch, return whether text[i+1..j] or text[i..j-1] is a palindrome.
solutions.pseudocode:
i = 0; j = n-1
while i < j: if t[i] != t[j]: return pal(i+1, j) or pal(i, j-1); i++; j--
return true
commonMistakes: Only trying to skip the left letter; 'cbbcc' needs the right one skipped.
Allowing a second skip inside the helper.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Two pointers walk inward while the ends match. At the first mismatch one of those two letters must go, so I check both remaining middles with a plain palindrome scan. There's only one branch point, so it's O(n) time and O(1) space.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.content: 'abca': a = a, then b ≠ c at i=1, j=2.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.content: Skip left: check text[2..2] = 'c', a palindrome. Return true.
